articles.title: Legacy Application Modernization: Prove Old and New Systems Agree
articles.excerpt: The safest way to finish a legacy application modernization is to run the old and new systems on the same real requests, compare every answer, and switch over only when every difference has been expla…
articles.body: The safest way to finish a legacy application modernization is to run the old and new systems on the same real requests, compare every answer, and switch over only when every difference has been explained and signed off. If your team can't show you that comparison, they're asking you to trust the rewrite on faith. You're probably here because a team has rebuilt something that matters, such as an order engine, a billing run or a pricing service, and now they want a date to switch off the old one. The demos look good and the test suite passes. But nobody can show you evidence that the new system gives the same answers on a normal Tuesday's real traffic. How do parallel runs and shadow traffic actually work?

articles.title: How to Test AI Workflows: Simple Evals in Python
articles.excerpt: A prompt gets one line of tweaking, and the assistant seems better. Or is it only that the three examples you tried happened to work this time? That's the trap with AI workflows. Ask the same question…
articles.body: A prompt gets one line of tweaking, and the assistant seems better. Or is it only that the three examples you tried happened to work this time? That's the trap with AI workflows. Ask the same question twice and you may get two different answers, so "it worked when I tried it" doesn't tell you much. This guide builds a small testing harness for exactly this problem. It runs your assistant over a set of example cases, checks the answers in flexible ways, repeats each case several times, and tells you how often it passes, with an honest idea of how sure that number is. It includes a stand-in assistant, so you can run everything offline, and the real model calls are a small step at the end. Why ordinary tests don't work A normal test says: given this input, expect exactly this output.

articles.title: 6 Delayed Webhook Tasks: Cron and Message Queues for Per-Event HTTPS Scheduling
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use a durable message queue for per-event webhook delays, and keep cron as a dispatcher for bounded recovery work. A public HTTPS endpoint should acknowledge quickly; it should not be th…
articles.body: Short answer: use a durable message queue for per-event webhook delays, and keep cron as a dispatcher for bounded recovery work. A public HTTPS endpoint should acknowledge quickly; it should not be the place where a long-running job waits. The useful design question is where each retry becomes durable and idempotent. I build B2B SaaS email, SMS, and OTP flows, so I pay attention to the unglamorous edges: rate limits, delivery gaps, and the moment a provider accepts a request while our process dies. Webhooks have the same shape. A timer can wake a process, but only a durable record can explain why an event is still owed. The six invariants I write down first For each outbound event, I keep an immutable event ID, a destination, a next-attempt timestamp, and an attempt count.

articles.title: Make IndexedDB upgrades atomic and recoverable
articles.excerpt: Why this matters IndexedDB schema changes aren’t just “make a new store” — they usually also move existing records into the new shape. If the browser aborts an upgrade after the destination is created…
articles.body: Why this matters IndexedDB schema changes aren’t just “make a new store” — they usually also move existing records into the new shape. If the browser aborts an upgrade after the destination is created but before every record is copied, your app can be left with a database that’s neither the old nor the new schema. What this pattern does Keep all structural work (create target store, copy records, remove source) inside the onupgradeneeded/versionchange callback so the browser’s versionchange transaction owns the entire move. Before copying records, write a durable migration marker that survives an abort. The marker is a recovery hint, not the migration itself.

articles.title: Solving the Password Audit Paradox: Why LLMs Need Sandboxed Local Processing
articles.excerpt: Most security audits involving Large Language Models (LLMs) fail immediately upon contact with reality. There is a fundamental tension between the utility of an AI agent—which needs context to provide…
articles.body: Most security audits involving Large Language Models (LLMs) fail immediately upon contact with reality. There is a fundamental tension between the utility of an AI agent—which needs context to provide insights—and the absolute requirement for privacy when handling sensitive credentials. If you want an AI to analyze your password hygiene, you face a binary choice that usually results in one of two failures: you upload your entire plaintext password vault to a cloud provider, effectively handing the keys to the kingdom to a third party; or you attempt to manually sanitize the data yourself, which defeats the purpose of using an automated agent in the first place.

articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.title: 'Let's all choose to make tomorrow better', Artemis II astronauts honored with Stephen Hawking Medal at Starmus
articles.excerpt: The Artemis II crew have joined an impressive list of honourees, including Buzz Aldrin, Jane Goodall and David Attenborough.
articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
